unmapped_findings: Strengthening-mechanism contributions for the AN800 (ANT800) specimen (Table 3): σ0 = 220 MPa (solid solution, incl. matrix friction stress), σg = 256 MPa (grain refinement), σd = 459 MPa (dislocation), σOrowan = 0 MPa (Orowan), giving theoretical σy = 935 MPa versus the measured YS = 968 MPa.

The Orowan strengthening contribution is 0 MPa for the Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si steel because the Al and Si additions suppress carbide formation, so no significant precipitation occurs; this holds for the whole test steel including AN800.

The Taylor factor of the AN800 specimen is 3.58 (the highest among AN750/AN800/AN850), alongside a GND density of 0.84×10^14 m^-2; AN800 reaches both the highest mean GND density and highest mean Taylor factor, giving it the largest dislocation-strengthening contribution.
Retained austenite in the annealed specimens is < 5 % and its strengthening contribution was neglected.
Across the three annealing conditions (750-850 °C) of the Fe-3Mn-2Al-0.25C-0.4Si alloy, the average error between predicted and measured YS was 1.56 %; this figure is not specific to ANT800 alone.
